newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end up on bond firming.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end up on bond firming.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended pit trading up on a late recovery in bonds after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged, as was expected.

Activity was muted by anticipation of Thursday's scheduled U.S. October consumer price index and retail sales reports. Forecasters looked for CPI to rise 0.3 percent and the core rate to gain 0.2 percent. October retail sales were expected to be up 0.3 percent overall and excluding autos.
Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended with no policy announcement, signalling no change in rates.
The discount rate remained at five percent and the Federal funds rate, which banks charge each other for overnight money, stayed at 5.25 percent.
Traders said stocks found renewed support from U.S. Treasury bond futures, which gradually erased most losses after the Fed's inaction and as the U.S. dollar advanced.
"There was no news from the Fed and the broader market has been strong all day," said one analyst.
The advance to the day's peak of 735.50 occurred on scanty turnover dominated by locals, characteristics that made some question the extent and durability of the rise.
"There was nothing for sale," added the analyst. "It was very thin."
Traders said to look for resistance at the contract high of 736.25, where they said buy stop orders would be triggered.
The market glossed over the October Atlanta Federal Reserve business activity index that fell to a -9.4 from a revised 3.4 in September.
Some brokers said the report was slightly weaker than expected and said the drop in the prices paid and received components might have helped support the market.

December S&P 500 futures closed up 2.15 points at 734.15; Value Line index futures up 3.60 at 667.30; New York Stock Exchange Composite index futures up 1.10 to 388.35; and the Russell 2000 index futures up 1.20 to 348.20. Nikkei Stock Average futures closed down 220.00 to 21,050.00.
